question.problem:
$$

Which of the following is equivalent to  $\operatorname{coth}⁡(\operatorname{ln}⁡2w)?$
question.worked_solution:
$$

The definition of $\operatorname{coth}⁡x$ is 

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{coth}⁡x & =\frac{1}{\operatorname{tanh}⁡x} \\  & =\frac{{e}^{x}+{e}^{-x}}{{e}^{x}-{e}^{-x}} \\  & =\frac{{e}^{2x}+1}{{e}^{2x}-1} \\  & =\frac{1+{e}^{-2x}}{1-{e}^{-2x}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Using the third definition, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{coth}⁡(\operatorname{ln}⁡2w) & =\frac{{e}^{2\operatorname{ln}⁡2w}+1}{{e}^{2\operatorname{ln}⁡2w}-1} \\  & =\frac{{e}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡4{w}^{2}}+1}{{e}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡4{w}^{2}}-1} \\  & =\frac{4{w}^{2}+1}{4{w}^{2}-1}.\end{aligned}
$$
